messages:
emily: FYI support ticket from MNC-42. Customers saw a ~3x provisional token spike after our quantized model rollout in eu-central. Looks like streaming reconnects + a mid-request model swap.

jess: any logs or sample session ids?

emily: session `sess_f9b2`, traced around 2026-03-02T11:12Z. console shows provisional +2.4k tokens then ledger corrected to +800 after 90s. Customers panic before correction.

caleb: found logs. The runtime swapped from `rwd-16g-fp16` -> `rwd-16g-q4` mid-stream because of autoscaler reshard during canary. Reconnect produced resumed chunks but our chunk accounting counted both pre and post swap offsets. snippet:
```
[2026-03-02T11:12:05Z] stream=session=sess_f9b2 model=rwd-16g-fp16 chunk_idx=12 tokens=128 state=active
[2026-03-02T11:12:06Z] autoscale=reshard node=us-eu-2 trigger=cpu model_swap=rwd-16g-q4
[2026-03-02T11:12:07Z] reconnect=session=sess_f9b2 resumed_chunk_idx=12 client_resume=true
[2026-03-02T11:12:07Z] ledger=provisional charge_tokens=128 entry_id=prov_734
```

nadia: so the router emitted a provisional for the resumed chunk even though the ledger already had a provisional from the original stream? why wasn't dedupe applied?

caleb: ledger dedupe runs on a (session, chunk_uuid) tuple but the chunk_uuid is regenerated on model swap because quantized runtime uses different chunk encoding. So ledger sees it as new.

jess: ugh. That means our dedupe depends on runtime chunk encoding staying stable across model variants. That seems brittle.

emily: customer-facing pain: console shows provisional high immediately. Even though final billed tokens are right, the UI behavior is causing CS tickets. We need short-term UI mitigation + longer-term server fix.

caleb: proposed approaches:
- make router/ledger dedupe use a stable fingerprint computed from original token offsets and prefix hash instead of runtime chunk_uuid
- or persist original chunk_uuid in session metadata so post-swap runtimes reuse it
- UI smoothing: treat provisional spikes for same session as potentially transient and delay showing to customers for X seconds with an opt-out toggle

jess: prefer stable fingerprint. Implementation idea (pseudo):
```
def stable_chunk_fingerprint(session_id, prefix_text, chunk_index):
    h = sha256((session_id + '|' + prefix_text[:1024] + '|' + str(chunk_index)).encode())
    return h.hex()[:16]
```
ledger would dedupe on that field if present.

caleb: caveat: stealing prefix_text into the ledger has PII risk. We could hash client-provided prefix server-side and only store fingerprint, not raw text. Also we must bound prefix length.

nadia: we also need to think about intentional client restarts that re-send same prefix vs clients that alter prompt to continue generation. Fingerprint should include a short rolling checksum of the first N tokens, not full text. N=64 tokens proposed.

billing-bot: alert: MNC-42 provisional_spike > $100 triggered at 11:13 UTC.

console-bot: note: dashboard PR #4310 (suppress-provisional-by-default) is awaiting review; currently behind feature flag `ui.provisional_smoothing`.

emily: action plan: short-term: jess enable `ui.provisional_smoothing` for MNC-42 and update support message. medium-term: caleb implement stable fingerprint in router + ledger, nadia lead runtime change to accept external chunk_fingerprint so different encodings can reuse same id.

jess: will flip flag for MNC-42 and add a help-text: "Console shows provisional estimates which may update; click to show provisional immediately." PR: https://git.internal/rw/console/pull/4310

caleb: I'll open a repo PR: https://git.internal/rw/ledger/pull/210 with proposed schema change: add field `stable_chunk_fingerprint` (string, nullable) and dedupe logic.

nadir: (typo) nadia: I'll draft runtime patch to accept `extern_chunk_fingerprint` on handoff. If runtime can't honor it we'll log an event `chunk_fingerprint_mismatch` for telemetry.

emily: let's also add a dashboard card to show recent model-swap handoffs per-customer so we can spot regressions during rollouts.

jess: putting owners: jess=ui, caleb=ledger+router, nadia=runtime, emily=customer comms. We'll canary ledger change to staging first.

caleb: note: we need migration strategy for existing provisional entries. ledger can compute stable_fingerprint from archived metadata for backfill, but that's lower priority.

emily: thanks team. keeping this thread open until MNC-42 confirms UI change and ledger patch exists in canary.
